# The same laptop after platform/k3d/estate.yaml pinned the Kubernetes API to
# 127.0.0.1:6445. Every remaining non-loopback listener is Apple's or the
# substrate's, and each has a row in catalog/ports.yaml saying so. bin/bind-audit
# must pass this. Loopback rows are included on purpose: the check must ignore
# them rather than count them as findings.
#
# 8080 was `*:8080` here until 2026-08-25, and it passed because bin/bind-audit
# carried its own process-name allow-list. Two changes killed that row. The
# ledger became the only allow-list, so the answer now comes from
# catalog/ports.yaml alone; and prospector#713 moved the edge to loopback, so
# ports.yaml (idp#28) declares `bind: 127.0.0.1` for 8080 and 8443. A fixture
# that still faced 8080 at the network was asserting a world that no longer
# exists, and the kernel agrees with the ledger:
#
#   $ lsof -nP -iTCP:8080 -sTCP:LISTEN
#   ssh  76583  chidionyema  13u  IPv4  ...  TCP 127.0.0.1:8080 (LISTEN)
COMMAND     PID        USER   FD   TYPE             DEVICE SIZE/OFF NODE NAME
